Teaching responsibilities will include upper- and lower-division art history courses at the undergraduate level: survey of art history, contemporary art theory and criticism, and courses per the candidate’s expertise, as well as a studio class as needed. The successful candidate will teach a 3/3 course load and manage the University’s Fine Arts Galleries. The three block teaching load per semester of this position falls within UM Western’s unique four block per semester system of experiential education called Experience One. Classes are experienced one at a time, and each class is taught as a three-and-a-half-week block (eighteen days). Faculty meet with students three regularly scheduled hours per day, A.M. or P.M. In addition to teaching three courses, one course/block non-teaching credit is given each semester for managing Western’s Fine Arts Galleries by coordinating two artist exhibitions, receptions, and lectures per semester in one gallery and rotating permanent collection works in the second gallery. Art history and criticism courses at Western introduce students to various cultures and cultural perspectives both contemporary and historical, including the artistic practices of non-Western societies. jobs.description: The Department of Geosciences in the W.A. Franke College of Forestry and Conservation (FCFC) at the University of Montana  (UM) invites applications for an Assistant Teaching Professor (non-tenure track) of Geoscience. We encourage applications from individuals with a passion for undergraduate education and high-impact learning practices, who can connect students with career opportunities in geosciences and related fields. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses to support the Geosciences degree, as well as other programs in the FCFC and at UM. Teaching responsibilities will include both in-person and online versions of a large undergraduate survey course in earth systems science with an associated lab, an earth systems science course for future educators, and a lower-division course in introductory surface processes. Other course assignments will be tailored to program needs and the strengths of the candidate and may include field methods, computational methods, writing, and other courses related to earth and environmental sciences. The Geosciences curriculum encourages field-based learning, and there are many opportunities for field instruction. There will also be opportunities for advising and supervision of undergraduate student research and contributions to departmental outreach and other service roles. The successful candidate will be hired on an academic year contract, with the opportunity to pursue additional compensation in the summer (such as formal summer teaching). The Department of Geosciences’ mission is to develop new knowledge regarding Earth's history, its environment and resources, engage our students in the process, and share that knowledge broadly. We have two areas of special focus: water and earth; in both areas, we teach and conduct research in an earth systems science context. jobs.description: The University of Montana invites applications for the position of Director and Professor / Associate Professor at the Flathead Lake Biological Station (FLBS). We seek an accomplished, visionary, and enthusiastic scholar to provide leadership for one of the world’s premier aquatic research and education facilities. The Director will guide FLBS’s research, education, and outreach programs, foster its national and international prominence in aquatic sciences, and strengthen the Station’s role as a vital contributor to the University of Montana and to the Flathead community. The Director of the Flathead Lake Biological Station lives in residence at FLBS as the chief academic and administrative officer of the Station and reports to the Vice President for Research at UM while maintaining a tenured appointment in a campus academic unit. The Director will provide visionary leadership to maintain and expand FLBS’s excellence in aquatic research, education, and outreach. This position is a full-time, residential 12-month academic and administrative leadership appointment supported by an experienced associate director. In addition to administrative duties at the station, the successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active research program and to engage in teaching consistent with the Director’s expertise, for example in FLBS’ summer session.
